cli.help.body:
commands:
  /help                 show this
  /setup                configure or repair the engine without closing Isaac
  /status               show session, workspace, model and usage
  /tools                list tools and allowed terminal commands
  /sessions             list saved CLI sessions
  /history              show this session's full conversation
  /show [n|last]        expand the full output of a collapsed command
  /log                  show this session's JSONL file
  /feedback             show how to rate the session/task
  /good [comment]       mark the last task as good
  /bad [comment]        mark the last task as bad
  /score 0-10 [text]    give the last task a numeric score
  /workspace [path]     show or change the working folder
  /model [profile|name] select model, reasoning effort and context
  /permissions          show the persistent authorizations that apply
  /mode                 switch between safe automatic and saved-only
  /language             change the interface language (it is saved)
  /clear                clear the conversation context
  /new                  end the current session and start another
  /exit                 quit

shortcuts:
  type / to search commands; arrows select and Tab completes
  Alt+Enter inserts a line break without sending the message
  Shift+Tab switches the command approval mode

examples:
  run git status
  look at the diff and tell me what is left to test
  commit the changes in this task with a short message
cli.feedback.body:
rating:
  /good [comment]        record that the last task was good
  /bad [comment]         record that the last task was bad
  /score 0-10 [comment]  record a numeric score

destination:
  raw feedback: {feedback}
  full session: {session}

later use:
  this does NOT go straight into Isaac's knowledge. A later task has to put
  these records through review and curation before distilling or fixing
  anything as learning.
